summary: Draft docs-first watchdog-default cluster record. The `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Power` `PowerWatchdog*TimeoutMsec` family has explicit repo-doc defaults under `InitializePowerWatchdogTimeoutDefaults`, but all five values are absent on the observed clean baseline and all five returned clean `no-hit` results in the broad current-build string batch. This keeps the cluster as a real research family, but still as a lower-priority docs-first hold rather than an active current-build RE lane.

setting.name: Control Power Watchdog Timeout Cluster
setting.casual_explanation: This cluster appears to define multiple watchdog timeout defaults inside the power manager. The values are documented in repo notes, but they are not present in the observed clean registry baseline.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel and power researchers may inspect these values when investigating watchdog timeout behavior around driver monitor, DWM sync flush, Po callouts, power-on GDI, and request queue paths.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The cluster has explicit doc defaults and clean baseline evidence, but it still lacks a current-build structural pivot. It is now on an intentional Ghidra/static hold because the current-build kernel image has no exact `PowerWatchdogTimeout` string match; it should stay in the research queue as a family hold, not a tweak candidate.
setting.professional_notes: The repo docs list five `Control\\Power` watchdog defaults under `InitializePowerWatchdogTimeoutDefaults`: `PowerWatchdogDrvSetMonitorTimeoutMsec = 10000`, `PowerWatchdogDwmSyncFlushTimeoutMsec = 30000`, `PowerWatchdogPoCalloutTimeoutMsec = 10000`, `PowerWatchdogPowerOnGdiTimeoutMsec = 30000`, and `PowerWatchdogRequestQueueTimeoutMsec = 30000`. The docs-first power routing pass already grouped them as new `Control\\Power` candidates. The observed clean baseline existence pass later confirmed that the parent `Control\\Power` path exists while all five registry values are absent. The broad current-build string batch then returned clean `no-hit` results for all five values, which is stronger than a vague unknown but still weaker than a real current-build symbol or caller clue. A later targeted host-side `ntoskrnl.exe` check also found no exact `PowerWatchdogTimeout` string; retained watchdog Ghidra artifacts are adjacent DPC/profile or Win32 callout evidence, not a direct reader/seeding path for this five-value `Control\\Power` cluster. Existing enrichment output already converges on the same next runtime family for all five values: `power-request-simulation`, low runtime priority, `windbg` queue. The cluster therefore deserves a schema-backed draft, but it is intentionally held until a targeted binary probe or new runtime trace provides a stronger current-build path-aware lead.
